triggers: a small-m Metal GEMV/GEMM cannot approach memory bandwidth
split-k GEMV stays far below MLX at decode shapes

payload.goal: Explain why scalar small-M Metal kernels cannot approach bandwidth and what does.

problem.statement: At m=16 the q4 GEMM is bandwidth-bound in theory (14-58 MB streamed once) but scalar-FMA implementations top out near 8 TFLOPS fp32-equivalent.

payload.what: Thread-per-column GEMV (with or without split-k) is limited by per-thread scalar FMA rate: measured 8.2 TFLOPS ceiling matches decode-qkv latency (14.8 GFLOP / 1.81 ms). Beating MLX at decode needs small-M MMA tiles plus split-k with an fp32 scratch and a reduce kernel; parallelism must come from k, not just n.
payload.when: Decode-shaped quantized GEMMs (m <= 32) where the incumbent still trails MLX.
payload.how: Split k into BKS-aligned chunks (chunk multiple of 32 keeps uint4 nibble loads aligned), write fp32 partials [split][column][row] to scratch, and reduce with a second kernel in the same command buffer or the next; keep the partial and reduce scratch layouts IDENTICAL.
caveats: thread-per-column GEMV parallelism is capped by n/threads_per_group threadgroups - 42 threadgroups cannot saturate a 32-core M5 Max

raw.seed: onyx-infer kernel-agent/q4-mma episodes E1-E8, ABBA-measured on Apple M5 Max (Mac17,14, Metal 4, metalfe-32023.921.6), 2026-11-17
